commitments.text: The Android client collects species, temperature, and free-text symptom description locally, and only submits a triage request when the operator explicitly starts analysis.
commitments.rationale: Mirrors DiagnoseScreen input collection before the VetNet call.

commitments.text: All client triage decisions must request the backend triage engine in real time before any diagnosis result is shown to the operator.
commitments.rationale: The current app computes diagnosis by calling VetNet.diagnose and does not host a client-side decision engine.

commitments.text: After a successful backend response, the client stores the symptom description, returned risk level, first suspected condition, and optional temperature in local Room tables.
commitments.rationale: MainActivity writes HistoryRecord and VitalRecord only inside the success callback.

commitments.text: When the network is unavailable, the client must lock the triage screen to prevent dirty data and incomplete reports from being treated as valid triage output.
commitments.rationale: The original workflow has no offline completion path and treats network failure as a hard stop.

commitments.text: A failed backend call ends the triage attempt with UI error feedback, and the client must not persist a diagnosis or pending report when no authoritative response was returned.
commitments.rationale: The error callback only surfaces a toast and leaves diagnosisResult unset.

commitments.text: The system depends on a single backend diagnosis engine; no secondary clinic node, replica, or embedded fallback engine participates in decision making.
commitments.rationale: VetNet is configured against one BASE_URL and no alternate authority exists in the mobile app.

commitments.text: Local Room storage is a record cache for history_table and vitals_table, not an authoritative triage decision source.
commitments.rationale: The app reads local history and recent temperatures, but diagnosis generation still depends on the backend call.

commitments.text: The client must not execute the multi-step triage tree offline or cache partially completed decision branches for later merge.
commitments.rationale: The current design contains no offline decision tree state, queue, or merge semantics.

commitments.text: Recent temperature history is rendered locally from vitals_table for dashboard display and does not trigger backend recomputation by itself.
commitments.rationale: HomeScreen reads the latest VitalRecord entries from Room LiveData.

commitments.text: The diagnosis engine accepts description, species, and optional temperature in one synchronous request and returns risk_level, suspected_conditions, rationale, and next_steps in one response.
commitments.rationale: This is the concrete request and response shape encoded in VetNet CaseRequest and DiagnosisResponse.

commitments.text: The first suspected condition from the backend response is persisted as the local condition summary shown in the history view.
commitments.rationale: MainActivity persists response.suspected_conditions.firstOrNull() as the condition field.

commitments.text: The client treats the backend response as the only valid diagnosis payload and does not merge server output with locally edited medical state.
commitments.rationale: The original design has no client-side conflict handling or multi-source reconciliation.

commitments.text: The v1 system has no background sync queue, no retry ledger, and no per-record version vector for triage data.
commitments.rationale: Neither the Android client nor the backend adapter model deferred writes or replicated history reconciliation.

commitments.text: Any loss of connectivity during triage blocks completion because the architecture couples diagnosis generation to immediate server availability.
commitments.rationale: The operator cannot obtain a result if VetNet fails.

commitments.text: The system assumes a single authoritative write path, so concurrent edits from another clinic are outside the v1 design envelope.
commitments.rationale: No multi-clinic or multi-writer protocol exists in the original implementation.

commitments.text: The mobile adapter is coupled to one HTTP diagnosis endpoint and one backend model runtime, which creates a single point of failure for all triage decisions.
commitments.rationale: VetNet configures exactly one BASE_URL and one OkHttp request path.

commitments.text: Because no pending report exists, operators must re-enter symptoms after a timeout or disconnect, increasing abandonment and data loss risk.
commitments.rationale: The app neither stores an offline draft nor resumes failed submissions.

commitments.text: Conflict resolution, offline report drafting, and multi-clinic replication are intentionally undefined in v1.
commitments.rationale: These gaps are exactly the seams that an offline-first evolution would need to redesign.

metadata.notes: Manual translation of the original petSystem online-first architecture. This is the approved seed baseline for future offline-first P10 evolution.
